summary: Modern databases and data platforms are increasingly embedding AI/ML directly into the data layer, allowing users to run inference, generate embeddings, and perform semantic (vector) search using SQL or native APIs without moving data to separate systems. Capabilities range from fully managed LLM functions (Snowflake Cortex, BigQuery ML with Vertex AI) to native vector indexes (MongoDB Atlas, Databricks Vector Search) and extension-based approaches (pgvector on PostgreSQL and Aurora). This convergence is driven by surging demand for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), with Gartner projecting 30% of enterprises will rely on vector-based retrieval for GenAI by 2026.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI (LLM functions, Cortex Search, Cortex Analyst)
databases.description: Cortex AI provides serverless SQL and Python functions for LLM inference (COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE, SENTIMENT, EXTRACT_ANSWER), embedding generation, and fully managed RAG via Cortex Search. It integrates hosted models from Anthropic, Meta, Mistral, and others, and Cortex is now extended to Snowflake Postgres for in-database AI.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake supports the VECTOR data type with VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY / L2 / inner-product functions, plus fully managed Cortex Search service for hybrid semantic + keyword retrieval.
databases.llm_integration: Built-in access to hosted foundation models (Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Snowflake Arctic) callable directly from SQL/Python via Cortex functions.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based; Cortex LLM functions billed per token (credits) and vector/search operations consume compute credits. No separate infrastructure to manage.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML with Vertex AI / Gemini integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets users create, train, and run ML models (regression, classification, clustering, time-series, deep learning) using standard SQL. It integrates with Vertex AI and Gemini for remote model inference, text generation (ML.GENERATE_TEXT), and embedding generation (ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING) directly in queries.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery provides the VECTOR_SEARCH function and CREATE VECTOR INDEX (IVF/TreeAH) for scalable approximate nearest-neighbor search over embedding columns.
databases.llm_integration: Tight integration with Vertex AI and Gemini models; remote models invoked via SQL functions like ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING.
databases.pricing_notes: On-demand (per TB scanned) or capacity-based (slots) for queries; remote model inference and embedding calls incur Vertex AI charges plus BigQuery compute.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector for embeddings and pgai/pgvectorscale for in-database AI workflows
databases.description: pgvector adds a vector data type and similarity operators to PostgreSQL, enabling embedding storage and ANN search. pgai (from Timescale) adds functions to generate embeddings and call LLMs (OpenAI, Ollama, etc.) from SQL, and pgvectorscale improves index performance for large-scale workloads.
databases.vector_search_notes: Extension-based but native-capable on open-source Postgres: vector search is provided by the pgvector extension (HNSW and IVFFlat indexes), not by core PostgreSQL. It is first-class once the extension is installed.
databases.llm_integration: Via the pgai extension, which calls external LLM/embedding providers (OpenAI, Cohere, Anthropic, Ollama) through SQL; also commonly used with LangChain.
databases.pricing_notes: Open-source and free; cost is the underlying compute/hosting plus any external LLM API usage. Managed providers (Timescale, Supabase, Neon) add hosting fees.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.description: Aurora ML allows SQL queries to invoke ML models hosted in Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock (including Comprehend for sentiment/entities) directly from Aurora PostgreSQL/MySQL, enabling inference and generative AI calls without exporting data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native to Aurora ML itself. Vector search on Aurora PostgreSQL is provided only through the third-party pgvector extension, which is separate from the Aurora ML service; Aurora ML focuses on model inference, not vector indexing.
databases.llm_integration: SQL functions invoke Amazon Bedrock foundation models and SageMaker endpoints; Comprehend integration for NLP tasks.
databases.pricing_notes: No extra charge for the Aurora ML feature itself; you pay standard Aurora compute/storage plus underlying SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend usage.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.description: Redshift ML lets users create, train, and deploy ML models using the CREATE MODEL SQL command, leveraging Amazon SageMaker Autopilot behind the scenes. It supports in-database inference and can invoke external SageMaker endpoints and Bedrock LLMs for generative AI from SQL.
databases.vector_search_notes: No native vector index/search as a core Redshift ML capability. Redshift has added limited vector similarity support, but there is no mature managed ANN vector index comparable to dedicated vector databases; vector search is not the focus of Redshift ML.
databases.llm_integration: SQL-based invocation of SageMaker-hosted models and Amazon Bedrock LLMs; built-in prediction functions from trained models.
databases.pricing_notes: No additional charge for the Redshift ML feature; you pay for Redshift compute/storage plus SageMaker training and any Bedrock inference costs.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI (model training, serving, agents) and Databricks Vector Search
databases.description: Mosaic AI provides end-to-end tooling for building, fine-tuning, serving, and evaluating ML and GenAI models, including Foundation Model APIs and agent frameworks. Databricks Vector Search is a managed vector database integrated with Unity Catalog and Delta tables for RAG.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a fully managed, built-in vector database that automatically syncs and indexes embeddings from Delta tables with governance via Unity Catalog.
databases.llm_integration: Mosaic AI Foundation Model APIs and Model Serving provide access to hosted and external LLMs (Llama, DBRX, OpenAI, Anthropic) plus fine-tuning and agent orchestration.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks Units (DBUs); Vector Search and Model Serving billed separately for compute and endpoint usage.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search and Atlas AI integrations
databases.description: Atlas Vector Search enables semantic similarity search over embeddings stored alongside operational JSON documents, supporting hybrid search and RAG. It integrates with frameworks like LangChain and LlamaIndex and embedding providers for building AI applications on operational data.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Vector search is built into Atlas via dedicated vector search indexes ($vectorSearch aggregation stage) using HNSW, with approximate and exact nearest-neighbor options and metadata filtering.
databases.llm_integration: No in-database LLM hosting, but tight integrations with OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, LangChain, and LlamaIndex for embedding generation and RAG pipelines.
databases.pricing_notes: Included with Atlas clusters on dedicated tiers; cost scales with cluster size/compute and storage for embeddings. External embedding/LLM API usage billed separately.
